curation.lead:
Kathryn H. Ruemmler served as White House Counsel to President Barack Obama from 2011 to 2014, one of the most sensitive positions in the executive branch. Within months of leaving government, she joined Latham & Watkins as a partner and simultaneously entered Jeffrey Epstein's orbit as his personal attorney, fiduciary, and closest female confidante. Over the next five years, she exchanged at least 201 emails with Epstein — making her his third most frequent correspondent in the DOJ Volume 11 corpus. Her formal legal engagement was structured not with Epstein personally but with Southern Trust Company, his USVI financial vehicle that held Deutsche Bank accounts exceeding $100 million (EFTA02492343). In August 2019, days before Epstein's death, she was named trustee of the Epstein 2019 Trust alongside Darren Indyke and Richard Kahn, and successor executor of his will (EFTA01266457).

The documentary record reveals a relationship that far exceeded conventional attorney-client boundaries. Epstein coached Ruemmler through every major career decision from 2014 to 2019: her withdrawal from consideration as U.S. Attorney General (EFTA02593429), her Latham compensation negotiations (EFTA02391492), her recruitment by Facebook where she routed a draft email to Sheryl Sandberg through Epstein for review (EFTA02503788), and her ultimate hiring at Goldman Sachs, where President John Waldron's recruiting emails were forwarded to Epstein (EFTA02633918). She shared deeply personal crises with him, forwarding accusatory emails from a romantic rival and receiving personal advice in return (EFTA02495705). Epstein provided a steady stream of gifts — an iMac, a 64-inch television, a Hermès Apple Watch, birthday flowers, Valentine's Day grooming services — consistent with his documented pattern of creating dependency through lavish personal attention.

Simultaneously, Ruemmler represented some of the most controversial figures in post-2016 American political life, with Epstein serving as the client broker. She represented George Nader, the convicted sex offender and Mueller investigation cooperating witness with ties to MBS, MBZ, and the Trump transition team (EFTA02502020). She represented Elliott Broidy in his Wall Street Journal hush-money scandal (EFTA02514715). Epstein offered her Hamad bin Jassim, the former Prime Minister of Qatar, as a client (EFTA02647898). She was introduced to Saudi intermediary Raafat Alsabbagh and met with Aziza Alahmadi in Washington on Epstein's coordination (EFTA02449625). She provided legal counsel to Ariane de Rothschild on the Edmond de Rothschild Bank 1MDB crisis, with Ariane confirming she had "3 of the top Lux law firms working for us + Yves + Kathy on all angles" (EFTA02455931). In April 2020, she became Goldman Sachs' Global Head of Regulatory Affairs — the bank that had paid $2.9 billion to settle 1MDB charges she had been monitoring since 2016. She resigned from Goldman in February 2026, shortly after the DOJ released the Epstein documents detailing the full scope of her involvement.

sections.title: Epstein as Career Architect
sections.content:
The email corpus documents Epstein's role as the central manager of Ruemmler's professional life from the moment she left the White House in 2014 through his arrest in July 2019. This pattern began with the most consequential decision of her career: the Attorney General nomination. In October 2014, Bloomberg reported that Obama was favoring Ruemmler to succeed Eric Holder. She forwarded the article to Epstein at 12:11 AM (EFTA02591681). Eight days later, she formally withdrew, sharing her statement with Epstein: "I have informed the President that I must decline his further consideration" (EFTA02593429). Whether Epstein's influence contributed to her withdrawal remains an open question, but the fact that he was the first person she notified — ahead of any public disclosure — reveals the primacy of the relationship.

Her September 2014 arrival at Latham & Watkins was likewise reported to Epstein in real time: "Chair of firm called and said Latham is 100% behind me whatever I decide to do" (EFTA02592389). By March 2016, she was negotiating her Latham compensation through Epstein: "What I need from Latham is a commitment on my compensation that goes beyond the numbers on the page" (EFTA02391492). When a Cravath partner left for Paul Weiss in April 2016, she told Epstein the Latham chair "now wants to meet with me," using the lateral move as leverage (EFTA02703473). Epstein reportedly claimed Paul Weiss had offered Ruemmler $6 million per year for three years.

The Facebook recruitment of 2018-2019 followed the same template. After Ruemmler told Epstein that Facebook was combining legal, policy, and communications under one executive reporting to Sheryl Sandberg (EFTA02583835), Epstein managed the courtship. When Sandberg called to offer her both the policy and general counsel roles (EFTA02604022), Ruemmler routed her follow-up email to Sandberg through Epstein for editing: "Hi Sheryl, I wanted to follow-up on my visit to FB last week" (EFTA02503788). Epstein even arranged for Richard Kahn to speak with Facebook VP Lori Goler about Ruemmler's compensation trust (EFTA02279339). When Ruemmler told Epstein "I'm done with FB" in April 2019, he counseled: "give them a shot and then turn it down" (EFTA02634912).

Goldman Sachs was the final transaction. Epstein had been tracking the opportunity since at least July 2017, asking "any goldman word!?" (EFTA02645320). When Goldman chose Karen Seymour for General Counsel in December 2017, Ruemmler told Epstein: "I totally called it! Goldman picked Karen Seymour from Sullivan & Cromwell, which I predicted from the very beginning" (EFTA02611782). The successful recruitment came in April 2019, when Goldman President John Waldron emailed Ruemmler: "We discussed again today in person as a leadership group. We are unified in wanting to make something work in short order" (EFTA02633918). She forwarded this to Epstein. Waldron separately told her, "Selfishly I am rooting for you to say no to the other opportunity" (EFTA02634941). Ruemmler joined Goldman as Global Head of Regulatory Affairs in April 2020 — nine months after Epstein's death.

sections.title: The Gulf State Client Nexus
sections.content:
Between 2016 and 2018, Epstein positioned Ruemmler at the intersection of all three major Gulf factions — Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Qatar — during the most volatile period in Gulf diplomacy. The timeline reveals a former White House Counsel simultaneously connected to opposing sides of the 2017 Gulf blockade, with Epstein as the common broker.

The Saudi thread began on October 2, 2016, when Epstein introduced Ruemmler to Raafat Alsabbagh with Aziza Alahmadi copied: "kathy - raafat, raafat - kathy" (EFTA02449625). Eleven days later, Alahmadi emailed Ruemmler directly about a "Meeting in Washington" with the note "See you on 15th" (EFTA02448016). By November 17, Alahmadi was sending a "List" to Epstein, who forwarded it to Ruemmler; she asked "Where are you meeting?" and Epstein replied "new york carib?" (EFTA02670134). This six-week sequence establishes that Ruemmler was actively meeting with Saudi contacts in Washington on a schedule coordinated through Epstein.

The UAE thread ran through George Nader, whom Ruemmler represented as attorney from at least March 2018. Richard Kahn emailed Epstein: "as i am sure you are aware, kathy is representing nadar" (EFTA02502020). Epstein confirmed this to Steve Bannon the following month: "as you know Kathy is Nader's counsel. she's very busy" (EFTA02479675). Nader was a key intermediary between MBS, MBZ, Erik Prince, and the Trump transition team. On October 17, 2018, Ruemmler forwarded Epstein a Rachel Maddow tweet showing a photograph of Nader with Saudi Crown Prince MBS — sharing media coverage of her own client's intelligence activities with her other client (EFTA02618825).

The Qatar thread emerged in June 2017, when Epstein directly asked Ruemmler about representing Hamad bin Jassim (HBJ), the former Prime Minister: "I assume you do not want to represent. Hamad bin jassim? Qatar. Hired Ashcroft. Silly, Anyone you would like to suggest for him?" Ruemmler asked: "Why does he need counsel?" Epstein replied: "Navigate wash views on intl law and sanctions" (EFTA02647898). That Epstein deemed John Ashcroft, a former U.S. Attorney General, "silly" as counsel for HBJ while considering Ruemmler the superior option reveals his assessment of her unique value: a former White House Counsel who reported to him.

The conflict crystallized in early 2018. On March 2, Ruemmler told Epstein she was "involved in the WSJ matter" — the Elliott Broidy hush-money scandal (EFTA02514715). Broidy was simultaneously a central figure in the Nader-Broidy anti-Qatar influence operation that would result in Broidy's FARA guilty plea. Ruemmler was thus representing Nader (UAE-aligned Mueller cooperator), Broidy (anti-Qatar Trump fundraiser), and had been offered HBJ (pro-Qatar former PM) as a client — all through the same broker, all at the same time. Whether these representations created actual legal conflicts of interest or were managed through appropriate ethical walls is unclear from the available documents, but the structural pattern is extraordinary.

sections.title: The Rothschild and 1MDB Deployment
sections.content:
Ruemmler's relationship with Ariane de Rothschild operated on two parallel tracks: a deep personal friendship and a professional deployment as crisis counsel for Edmond de Rothschild Bank during the 1MDB scandal. The three — Epstein, Ruemmler, and Rothschild — formed a social triangle documented across dozens of emails. They traveled together in Paris on July 4, 2015, met at Epstein's mansion, and socialized extensively. Epstein listed them together in May 2015: "ruemmler, leon, mort, rosvky, ariane ??!!" (EFTA02718629). Ruemmler shared insider banking intelligence with Epstein, reporting that "Yves is leaving Ariane's bank and going to EFG" (EFTA02617323).

The professional deployment began in March 2016, when Epstein proposed giving Ruemmler "point authority on luxembourg" for the Rothschild bank's remediation strategy in the 1MDB scandal (EFTA02468553). By July 2016, Ariane confirmed Ruemmler's central role: "I have 3 of the top Lux law firms working for us + Yves + Kathy on all angles" (EFTA02455931). The fee structure was negotiated between Epstein and Ariane, with Epstein proposing that "ariane pays southern trust (my co). based on final settlement with DOJ" — a contingency arrangement with payments ranging from $5 million to $25 million depending on the settlement amount (EFTA02493823). This meant Ruemmler's work for the Rothschild bank was being billed through Epstein's Southern Trust Company, not through Latham & Watkins directly.

On September 2, 2016, Ruemmler sent Epstein a Sarawak Report article: "90 Federal Police Officers Raided Edmond de Rothschild Bank! How Aabar Scandal Could Dwarf 1MDB" (EFTA02452636). This monitoring continued through 2018. The significance deepened retroactively when Ruemmler became Goldman Sachs' Global Head of Regulatory Affairs in April 2020. Goldman had paid $2.9 billion to settle its own 1MDB charges, and Ruemmler now appeared in CourtListener records for both US v. Leissner (1:18-cr-00439, EDNY) and US v. Goldman Sachs Malaysia (1:20-cr-00438, EDNY). She had been tracking 1MDB from inside Epstein's network since 2016, advising the Rothschild bank on its exposure, and then took the top regulatory role at the most heavily penalized bank in the scandal.

sections.title: Epstein Legal Defense Strategy
sections.content:
Ruemmler served as Epstein's lead strategic attorney at Latham & Watkins from 2014 through at least 2019, handling the most sensitive legal matters in his portfolio. Her engagement was formally with Southern Trust Company rather than with Epstein personally — a legally significant distinction that Epstein himself clarified when Ruemmler asked about the engagement letter: "Do you mean the engagement letter between Latham and the bank?" Epstein replied: "no, the letter engaging southern trust co to work, (me)" (EFTA02492343). This corporate veil placed Latham's client of record as an Epstein entity with Deutsche Bank balances exceeding $100 million, rather than a convicted sex offender.

Her legal work centered on the Boies/Virginia Roberts litigation from 2015 through 2018. In October 2015, she connected Laura Menninger (Ghislaine Maxwell's attorney) with Darren Indyke and reached out to David Boies directly (EFTA02355170). She forwarded a $50,000 retainer request for Maxwell's legal fees to Epstein (EFTA02484900). She engaged substantively with the defense theory, questioning whether "Boies would put himself so out there if he knew he had been scammed by virginia" and Epstein asked her to "sit with Boies and make that point" (EFTA02463902). When Boies sent settlement documents in December 2018, Ruemmler asked sharp strategic questions: "What are terms? He has already spoken publicly about cases against you in attempt to rehab his rep after Harvey. Can he claim victory for his client publicly after settlement?" (EFTA02611830). She also assessed media strategy, attributing a February 2017 Politico article about the Epstein-Acosta plea deal to Boies: "Fed to reporter by Boies, I'm sure" (EFTA02660014).

Beyond the Roberts litigation, Ruemmler discussed the Non-Prosecution Agreement as "highly improper" and strategized defense arguments including "weakness of fed jurisdiction." She forwarded executed NPAs for Rothschild and Credinvest banks to Epstein. Her involvement with Ken Starr, who had helped negotiate Epstein's original 2008 plea deal, is documented in the corpus (EFTA02613558), as is her coordination with Abbe Lowell, Jared Kushner's attorney, with whom she discussed the Kushner defense for an hour in November 2017 (EFTA02571471). The breadth of her legal coordination — spanning victim litigation, NPA defense, Maxwell strategy, and political-legal intelligence — placed her at the center of Epstein's defense architecture.

sections.title: Personal Relationship and Leverage Dynamics
sections.content:
The documentary record reveals an intimacy between Ruemmler and Epstein that extended far beyond professional counsel. In September 2014, during UN General Assembly week, Ruemmler asked Epstein "girls?" in a text exchange. Epstein replied: "careful i will renew an old habit," then pivoted to listing his VIP roster for the week: "thiel, summers, bill burns, gordon brown, jagland, mongolia pres, hardeep puree (india), boris (gates), jabor (qatar), sultan (dubai), kosslyn (harvard), leon black, woody." Ruemmler responded: "Most girls do not have to..." with the sentence continuing across multiple documents (EFTA02366985, EFTA02518446, EFTA02518587). This exchange represents one of the most direct references in the corpus to Ruemmler's awareness of Epstein's activities with women.

In June 2015, Ruemmler shared a deeply personal crisis with Epstein. Cheryl Gould, an NBC News Vice President, sent Ruemmler accusatory messages: "Reid has confessed his secrets and lies. He has told me that his relationship [with Ruemmler]..." and "He has also told me that he is happy being married to me, loves me completely, and would never want to spend his life with you." Ruemmler immediately forwarded these to Epstein on both June 13 and June 15, 2015 (EFTA02495705, EFTA02338198, EFTA02353432). Epstein told Ruemmler to "call me again" (EFTA02499318). This pattern — sharing the most sensitive personal vulnerabilities with Epstein — mirrors Lawrence Summers sharing his own relationship crisis with Epstein in March 2019. Both dynamics gave Epstein leverage through intimate knowledge of their private lives.

Epstein maintained the relationship through a systematic program of gift-giving and personal attention. In November 2015, he bought Ruemmler an iMac for her New York apartment and a 64-inch television for her DC residence, dispatching his personal technician "James" to set up equipment at both her apartment and her Latham & Watkins office (EFTA00335003, EFTA00335051). In November 2018, a Hermès Apple Watch: "Of course, I love the Hermes one! If truly okay with him to do the Hermes, I would love the 40 mm, stainless Hermes with bleu indigo swift leather double tour" (EFTA02262535). He sent birthday flowers from Roses and Blooms every April 19 (EFTA02240847), wine deliveries in February (EFTA02276922), Paul Simon concert tickets (EFTA02486703), and arranged Valentine's Day "Glam Squad" sessions through Lesley Groff for "Karyna, Mel, Kathy Ruemmler" (EFTA02238367). Epstein visited her Mott Street apartment in Nolita with his driver on December 1, 2018, inspecting living arrangements that Latham & Watkins was subsidizing as part of her compensation (EFTA02264573, EFTA02615988).

sections.title: The Mansion Nexus and Political Intelligence
sections.content:
Ruemmler was a frequent presence at Epstein's 9 East 71st Street Manhattan mansion, attending meetings that mixed political figures, legal strategists, and Epstein's financial contacts. On May 19, 2017, she met at the mansion with Brad Karp, Chairman of Paul Weiss, who "will join the Kathy Ruemmler meeting tomorrow at 5:30pm" (EFTA02212889). On April 5, 2019 — three months before Epstein's arrest — Ruemmler, Bannon, and Anthony Scaramucci held a joint meeting at the mansion (EFTA02280625). The September 2018 schedule shows three separate Epstein self-reminders about "ruemmler" on the same day, suggesting intensive planning for her visits (EFTA02622553).

Beyond the mansion gatherings, Ruemmler served as an informal political and legal intelligence channel. She provided running commentary on the Trump administration: his financial disclosures were "silly, include revenues of hotels as INCOME. no related expenses" (EFTA02647281); his hiring of John Dowd prompted "Omg. John Dowd???" (EFTA02647260); the firing of Sally Yates drew immediate analysis. She tracked SEC enforcement activity, reporting that the SEC was "looking further into whether musk tried to manipulate the stock to punish the shorts" (EFTA02622716). She also served as Epstein's bridge to Israeli intelligence-connected client Amit Kochavi, with a forwarded article noting: "And now Kochavi has purchased the services of President Obama's former White House counsel, Ruemmler, whose name was once on the shortlist for US attorney general" (EFTA02358899). This intelligence-sharing role extended the value of Ruemmler's government background well beyond legal counsel, making her a real-time source on regulatory, judicial, and political developments.

sections.title: Trust, Estate, and Aftermath
sections.content:
The most legally significant marker of Ruemmler's position in the Epstein network is her designation in his estate documents. The 2019 Trust names "DARREN K. INDYKE, RICHARD D. KAHN, and KATHERYN H. RUEMMLER, as Trustees" (EFTA01266457). Epstein's will appoints "KATHRYN H. RUEMMLER, as successor Executor" (EFTA01266278). An additional trust instrument names her as successor trustee (EFTA01266434). These fiduciary designations place Ruemmler in the absolute inner core of Epstein's legal and financial structure — alongside Indyke and Kahn, who had served Epstein for decades — not merely as an external advisor but as someone entrusted with ongoing authority over his assets after death.

Ruemmler joined Goldman Sachs as Global Head of Regulatory Affairs in April 2020, approximately eight months after Epstein's death. FEC records confirm the employment transition: contributions list her employer as Latham & Watkins through 2019 and Goldman Sachs from 2020 onward. At Goldman, she made substantial political contributions: $10,000 to the DNC (September 2020), $10,000 to the Biden Victory Fund (September 2020), $6,600 to Harris for President (July 2024), and $5,000 annually to the Goldman Sachs PAC (2020-2025). Her most recent contribution (May 2025, $5,000 to GS PAC) listed her occupation as "investment banker" rather than attorney, suggesting an expanded role. SEC EDGAR confirms her name appears in Goldman Sachs DEF 14A proxy statements from 2022 through 2024. Despite her former White House Counsel status and extensive government-adjacent advisory work, she has zero appearances as a registered lobbyist in Senate LDA records.

In February 2026, Ruemmler resigned from Goldman Sachs, as confirmed by a LittleSis entity update. Her departure coincided with the DOJ's release of Epstein documents that detailed the full scope of her involvement in his legal strategy, estate planning, and career management. The timing follows a pattern observed with other Epstein-connected figures — departures from institutional positions following document releases — though no causal link has been established.
